target_profile.system_boundary: Single Go module github.com/imdea-software/swiftpaxos. The audited responsibility is the EPaxos replica package epaxos/ (epaxos.go, defs.go, exec.go) together with the shared replica/, state/ and rpc/ helpers it calls. A replica process is launched by run.go (runReplica) with protocol epaxos; the module also contains sibling protocols (swift, curp, n2paxos, paxos, fastpaxos) that are not part of this run's analysis roots.
protocol_contexts: epaxos replica process: peer-to-peer RPC over TCP, per-peer reader goroutines, a single run() select loop dispatching Prepare/PreAccept/Accept/Commit/TryPreAccept and their replies
client propose/stat connections handled by replica.clientListener into ProposeChan
master registration supplying ReplicaId and the peer address list (run.go registerWithMaster)
external_interfaces: client/buffer.go and client/client.go: request generation, pipelining and reply matching (not read this turn)
master/master.go: participant configuration, supplies nodeList and isLeader
master Register/GetLeader/GetReplicaList RPC used by runReplica
peer TCP byte stream carrying the RPC table ids defined in epaxos/defs.go
ownership: instance identity is (Replica, Instance); there is no global leader, term or log
each replica owns its own row of instances (crtInstance/CommittedUpTo/ExecedUpTo/conflicts are per replica)
any replica can become the leader of an existing instance during recovery by raising the ballot
selection_injection: protocol selection: run.go runReplica switch on c.Protocol == epaxos
epaxos.New arguments from run.go: exec = !c.Noop, beacon = false, durable = false, batchWait = 0, transconf = false, failures = (N-1)/2
replica.New hardcodes Thrifty = true, Dreply = true, Beacon = false, Durable = false; epaxos.New then overwrites Beacon and Durable from its own arguments
quorum.conf, latency.conf and aws.conf supply quorum sets and injected per-peer delays (replica/defs/latency.go)
variants: N = len(peerAddrList); F = failures; FastQuorumSize = F + (F+1)/2, SlowQuorumSize = (N+1)/2
Thrifty true for the launched configuration
N <= 3 with Thrifty disables the fast-path attribute-equality check
transconf false, Durable false and batching disabled in the launched configuration
unknowns: client/buffer.go and client/client.go were not read; the exact completion contract observed by clients (which replies are awaited, what a retry does) is unknown
master/master.go was not read; whether it can change the participant set or the recorded leader while replicas run is unknown

activities.purpose: Form a per-instance decision: fix the command, its sequence number and its dependency vector, and advance the instance from tentative pre-accept through accept to commit.
activities.realization_summary: handlePropose allocates (r.Id, ++crtInstance[r.Id]) and startPhase1 derives the initial (seq,deps) from the local conflict tables, records the instance as PREACCEPTED and broadcasts PreAccept to FastQuorumSize-1 preferred peers (Thrifty). handlePreAccept recomputes attributes on the receiver and replies with (bal,vbal,seq,deps,CommittedUpTo,status). handlePreAcceptReply merges replies and commits on the fast path when preAcceptOKs >= FastQuorumSize-1 and allEqual and (for N>7) allCommitted and the ballot is the initial ballot; otherwise the instance moves to ACCEPTED and a majority accept round runs in handleAcceptReply (acceptOKs+1 > N/2), followed by bcastCommit.
variants: Thrifty fast quorum versus full broadcast
N<=3 and Thrifty skip the attribute-equality check
N>7 propagates committedDeps and can make the fast path fail on allCommitted
batching when batchWait > 0 (disabled by run.go)
unknowns: whether skipping the equality check for N<=3 with Thrifty is compensated by another mechanism

activities.purpose: Carry the per-instance authority context: which ballot the record is promised to, at which ballot its attributes were last fixed, and which replica may currently advance it.
activities.realization_summary: Each Instance keeps bal (highest ballot promised) and vbal (ballot at which the current attributes were established). maxRecvBallot is raised by every received message type and constrains makeBallot, which picks id + k*N, shifted by another N when the replica is not the instance owner and further raised while IsLeader. Ballot comparison gates every message and reply: lower ballots are dropped or nacked, and a majority of nacks lets a replica raise the ballot and run prepare. Ownership of the instance row never moves, but the right to lead it does.
variants: initial ballot equals the owner replica id
recovery ballot for a non-owner is shifted by N
unknowns: whether any in-repository caller other than a nack majority ever sets IsLeader

activities.purpose: Re-establish eligible participation for an instance that is blocking execution by reconstructing its attributes and value from a majority.
activities.realization_summary: executeCommands times out an instance that has stayed uncommittable for COMMIT_GRACE_PERIOD (10s) and pushes instancesToRecover; startRecoveryForInstance returns early when the local record is already committed with commands, otherwise it seeds LeaderBookkeeping from the local record and broadcasts Prepare. handlePrepareReply waits for SlowQuorumSize replies at the current ballot, takes the attributes of the highest vbal and selects sub-case 1..6 (already committed, accepted, pre-accepted with enough equal support, weaker pre-accepted support, restart phase 1 with the recovered or NOOP command).
variants: sub-case dispatch order documented in handlePrepareReply
TryPreAccept path started from sub-case 4
defer-cycle guard using possibleQuorum
unknowns: which sub-case condition the comment lines describe, given that sub-cases 3 and 4 carry identical guards today

activities.purpose: Define participant eligibility and quorum arithmetic: who is a member, who is believed alive, and how many equal or majority supports are needed.
activities.realization_summary: N and F come from the peer address list and the master-visible participant count; FastQuorumSize = F + (F+1)/2, SlowQuorumSize = (N+1)/2, WriteQuorumSize = F+1, ReadQuorumSize = N-F. Alive[] is set during connection setup and cleared by replicaListener when a peer reader fails; PreferredPeerOrder (from ComputeClosestPeers or the latency table) decides which FastQuorumSize-1 peers and which majority peers receive PreAccept/Accept/Commit.
variants: Thrifty subset selection versus full broadcast
injected per-peer delays from the latency file
unknowns: whether a peer whose reader failed is ever re-admitted, since Alive is only cleared in the listener

activities.purpose: Apply committed instances to the replicated state machine in one order and complete the client-visible operation.
activities.realization_summary: executeCommands scans rows in replica order and instances in increasing order from ExecedUpTo+1, requires Status == COMMITTED, computes the strongly connected component of the dependency graph reachable from the candidate, and executes every instance of that component in increasing (Seq, owner replica, proposeTime) order; each executed instance is marked EXECUTED and ExecedUpTo advances only over contiguous prefixes. Client replies are produced during execution when a proposal is still attached (Dreply true), otherwise at commit time.
variants: transconf block in strongconnect (inert as written)
Dreply true (replies on execute) versus false (replies on commit)
unknowns: whether per-row ordering of non-conflicting commands is required by any consumer

activities.purpose: Retain the local history later decisions depend on: per-key conflict indexes, watermarks, and when enabled a durable record.
activities.realization_summary: conflicts[q][key] holds last (any op) and lastWrite (non-GET) instance numbers per replica, and maxSeqPerKey holds the highest sequence seen per key; both are updated at proposal, at pre-accept on the receiver and at commit. CommittedUpTo and ExecedUpTo are contiguous-prefix watermarks over the instance rows. recordInstanceMetadata/recordCommands/sync write a stable-store record when Durable is set; run.go always passes durable = false.
variants: Durable false (launched configuration) makes the stable-store path inert
conflict tables are never cleared after process start
unknowns: no reader of the stable store exists in the captured snapshot, so the record layout has no in-repo consumer

activities.purpose: Define when a client-visible operation is complete and how a proposal survives a leader or replica change.
activities.realization_summary: A client connection writes Propose records into a delayed channel; the replica attaches the writer, mutex and proxy flag to a GPropose and answers either during execution (Dreply true) or at commit (!Dreply), using ReplyProposeTS with the original CommandId and Timestamp. Pending proposals are kept in LeaderBookkeeping.clientProposals so a recovered instance can still answer them, and a NOOP commit on the owner's own row re-proposes the pending proposals onto ProposeChan.
variants: Dreply true versus false
NOOP re-proposal only when commit.Replica == r.Id
unknowns: whether a client can observe a reply for a proposal whose command was replaced by NOOP

facts.meaning: For instance (Replica, Instance) a replica holds one record carrying bal, vbal, Cmds, Seq, Deps and Status, and that record is the only local input to that replica's decision and execution for the instance.

identity.instance: instance number within the owner row

facts.validity_context: valid from the moment the slot is created (default NONE record, proposal, or any received message) until a later message raises bal or installs new attributes; Status is monotone in the normal path but bal, vbal, Seq and Deps can be replaced by a higher ballot or by a commit.
representation: epaxos.Instance fields Cmds, bal, vbal, Status, Seq, Deps
epaxos.LeaderBookkeeping fields ballot, status, cmds, seq, deps, originalDeps, committedDeps
facts.durability: durable only when the Durable flag is set; run.go launches the epaxos replica with durable = false, so the record lives in process memory and is lost on restart.
facts.recovery: rebuilt by running prepare for the instance and adopting the attributes reported with the highest vbal among a slow quorum of replies.
unknowns: whether replacing bal, vbal, Seq and Deps on a record that already stored accepted attributes can lose an accepted value a later recovery depends on

facts.meaning: Instance (Replica, Instance) is committed at a replica with a specific (Cmds, Seq, Deps, bal, vbal) vector, and that vector is the one execution must apply.

identity.ballot: commit.Ballot for followers, lb.ballot for the deciding leader

facts.validity_context: established by the leader's fast or slow path decision or by installing a Commit message; consumed by executeCommands and by recovery replies, where a committed record short-circuits further recovery.
representation: Commit message (LeaderId, Replica, Instance, Ballot, Command, Seq, Deps)
facts.durability: not durable in the launched configuration; a restarted replica must relearn commitment from peers.
facts.recovery: recovered by prepare; a reply with status >= COMMITTED makes sub-case 1 re-install the committed attributes on the recovering leader, which then re-broadcasts commit.
unknowns: whether every ordering of committed attributes a follower can install is also reachable as a decision by some quorum

facts.meaning: ExecedUpTo[q] is the highest instance of row q such that every instance (q, 0..ExecedUpTo[q]) has been applied, and CommittedUpTo[q] is the analogous committed prefix.
facts.validity_context: maintained by executeCommands and updateCommitted; only advanced across contiguous executed or committed records.
facts.durability: not durable in the launched configuration.
facts.recovery: rebuilt by execution and by the recovery timeout path, which enqueues the whole suffix starting at the blocked instance.

facts.meaning: conflicts[q][key] records the highest instance of row q known to have touched key (any operation) and to have written it; maxSeqPerKey[key] records the highest sequence number attached to key.
facts.validity_context: updated when a proposal is created, when a command is pre-accepted on a receiver, and when a commit is installed; it is a local over-approximation of what this replica has seen.
facts.durability: not durable in the launched configuration.
facts.recovery: rebuilt only from messages this process receives after restart; a restarted replica starts with empty conflict tables and an empty instance space.
unknowns: whether a restart with empty instance space and empty conflict tables is a supported configuration

facts.meaning: An unanswered client proposal is attached to the instance created for it and stays attached across accept, commit install and recovery until the replica answers it.
facts.validity_context: created by handlePropose, preserved by startRecoveryForInstance, consumed by ReplyProposeTS or by the NOOP re-proposal path.
representation: LeaderBookkeeping.clientProposals, each a GPropose with Reply writer, Mutex, Proxy and Addr
facts.durability: not durable; a restart loses the client writer.
facts.recovery: a committed NOOP on the owner's row re-proposes the pending proposals onto ProposeChan and clears the list.
unknowns: whether the re-proposal path can duplicate a command that was already committed

facts.meaning: Among a slow quorum of PrepareReplies the attributes carried with the highest vbal are the ones a recovering leader must re-propose; attributes reported with a lower vbal are stale.
facts.validity_context: used inside handlePrepareReply while choosing the value to re-propose; the bal and vbal promises recorded by acceptors are what make the comparison meaningful.
facts.durability: depends on the in-memory record; not durable in the launched configuration.
facts.recovery: is itself the mechanism used to reconstruct the value.
unknowns: whether the recovering leader's own record is adequately represented when its vbal was just overwritten with the new ballot

facts.meaning: The stable store receives a header of 9 + 4N bytes followed by marshalled commands for each recorded instance metadata write.
facts.validity_context: only written when Durable is true; the launched configuration passes durable = false, so this fact is never produced in the default deployment.
representation: bytes written by Replica.recordInstanceMetadata for one instance with distinct bal, vbal, Status and Seq: 04030201|03|100f0e0d|deps in the confirmed run (vbal at offset 0, no bal)
facts.durability: this is the durability mechanism itself.
facts.recovery: no in-repository reader exists, so nothing reconstructs state from these bytes.
unknowns: the confirmed check for claim C2-durable-record-preserves-written-fields shows the produced record does not carry the value written for bal and places Status inside the bytes a reader would use for vbal; whether an external reader's expected offsets differ from that remains unread

the repository README asserts that the bundled EPaxos is the corrected version and that thriftiness is required for correct recovery; it is project documentation, not a verification source.

channel-based sender helper (Sender channel type with Send* methods) defined in the shared replica package; no caller outside its own file was found in the snapshot, so it carries no responsibility for the epaxos path.

message-set helper (MsgSet with quorum-based Add/Free) defined in the shared replica package; no caller outside its own file was found in the snapshot, so it carries no responsibility for the epaxos path.

the value and command wire codecs frame every command a replica sends or receives; they carry no protocol decision, but the direct checks for claim C10-command-value-length-survives-the-wire confirmed that a value beyond the two-byte length field is silently shortened while its bytes remain in the stream, that the next command decodes to garbage, and that a real PreAccept carrying such a value makes the receiver's decoder panic, which the default 1000-byte command size does not reach (S37-state-value-codec, S38-client-command-size, S22-replica-listener).

formation.explanation: A command becomes a decision in two stages. First the owner replica allocates instance (r.Id, ++crtInstance[r.Id]) in handlePropose and startPhase1 derives the initial (seq, deps) from its conflict index and maxSeqPerKey, stores the record as PREACCEPTED, and broadcasts PreAccept to FastQuorumSize-1 preferred peers under thrifty or to all peers otherwise. Second each recipient validates the ballot against its own promise, recomputes (seq, deps) from its own conflict index while skipping the owner's own row when the recipient is not the owner, stores the command with status PREACCEPTED_EQ when nothing changed and PREACCEPTED when it did, and replies with (bal, vbal, Seq, Deps, CommittedUpTo, Status). The leader counts only replies whose ballot equals lb.lastTriedBallot, merges them with mergeAttributes (reply-wise maximum plus an equality flag), and commits immediately when preAcceptOKs >= FastQuorumSize-1 and the replies agreed and, for N>7, the merged deps are known committed, and the ballot is the initial ballot. Otherwise it records ACCEPTED, broadcasts Accept to a majority (N/2 peers when thrifty, all peers otherwise), counts acceptOKs and commits at acceptOKs+1 > N/2. The decision is then propagated as a Commit to every peer, which installs (Cmds, Seq, Deps, bal, vbal) and status COMMITTED.

context.explanation: The authority context of an instance is a pair of ballots on the per-instance record: bal is the highest ballot promised to any leader for that instance and vbal is the ballot at which the record's current attributes were established. Every handler raises maxRecvBallot, and makeBallot derives the next ballot as id + k*N, shifted by another N when the replica is not the instance owner and raised past maxRecvBallot while IsLeader is set. Lower-ballot messages are dropped or answered without lowering a promise; a reply with a ballot higher than lb.lastTriedBallot counts as a nack, and once nacks exceed N>>1 an IsLeader replica makes a new ballot and runs prepare. Ownership of the instance row never moves, but the right to lead the instance does: startRecoveryForInstance, triggered by the execution timeout, rebuilds LeaderBookkeeping from the local record, raises bal and vbal to the new ballot and prepares against a slow quorum. The recovering leader then keeps the attributes reported with the highest vbal and either commits, accepts, try-pre-accepts, or restarts phase 1 with the recovered command or with NOOP when no command is known. In the captured implementation the recovering replica also raises its own record's vbal to the newly made ballot before it builds its PrepareReply, so the resolution's running maximum starts above any value that other replicas accepted at older vbals; the direct checks for claim C1-recovery-adopts-committed-vector confirmed in scope that this lets a recovery commit a NOOP vector for an instance another replica already holds as COMMITTED with a real command, and that the recoverer's Commit broadcast does not repair the disagreement; the strongest of those checks drives the committed record itself from a real proposal, PreAccept round and commit broadcast before the recovery runs. The same masking holds when the recovering replica is the replica the deployment promoted to leader (IsLeader true, so makeBallot raises the new ballot past maxRecvBallot): the promoted-variant check for claim C6-recovery-ignores-committed-reply-when-promoted confirmed in scope that the committed reply is still skipped and the NOOP vector committed, and the accept handler's own rejection branch for a higher-ballot AcceptReply is unreachable because the ballot-equality gate returns first (claim C7-accept-reply-higher-ballot-is-a-rejection, confirmed in scope), so a rejected round waits for the timeout-driven recovery.

connection.explanation: The two lines meet at the per-instance record. Formation consumes the dependency and sequence facts the conflict index (A6) establishes and produces the committed attribute vector; the authority line decides which candidate vector may be adopted, because a higher ballot lets a new leader re-propose but the value it must re-propose is selected by vbal. The support that stays eligible across a change of leader is therefore the highest-vbal reply among a slow quorum rather than the local record, and the support that a follower keeps is what it already stored for that instance. Once a record is COMMITTED with commands, recovery short-circuits (startRecoveryForInstance returns early) and later Commit messages for that instance are ignored, so established decisions constrain subsequent formation; a PreAccept for a record whose status is already >= ACCEPTED is deliberately not recomputed so accepted attributes are not regressed, and a lower-ballot PreAccept is dropped. Pending client proposals are carried in the leader bookkeeping across the transfer and are re-proposed when a NOOP commit lands on the owner's row. Old replies are rejected solely by ballot comparison, which is the only correlation between a reply and the round it belongs to. Execution (A5) closes the loop: it waits for every dependency instance to be COMMITTED, collapses cycles into one SCC executed in Seq order, and advances the contiguous watermarks that later proposals and recovery replies advertise through CommittedUpTo. Progress when a round is rejected does not come from the handlers: the direct check for claim C8-timeout-enqueues-blocked-instance confirmed that the executor's per-row timeout enqueues the blocked instance for recovery after roughly twelve seconds of wall clock, so a stalled row is recovered by the timeout path rather than by a rejection signal.

open_details: handlePreAccept's status >= ACCEPTED branch stores the incoming command in InstanceSpace[preAccept.LeaderId][Instance] while every other access in the same handler uses preAccept.Replica (S9-handlePreAccept). Source review of every status-advancing path found no state with Status >= ACCEPTED and Cmds == nil: acceptors keep Status NONE, the leader-side accept/commit paths copy commands, and the only nil-Cmds records are fresh defaults with Status NONE. The wrong-slot write is therefore unreachable while acceptors do not record acceptance; the unprotected premise is whether handleAccept is required to record ACCEPTED (S11-handleAccept, S12-handleAcceptReply, S13-handleCommit).

handleAccept stores Deps, Seq, bal and vbal but never records an ACCEPTED status, so a replica in the accept quorum that never saw the PreAccept keeps Status NONE; the >= ACCEPTED guards in handlePreAccept and findPreAcceptConflicts therefore only ever see COMMITTED on non-leaders (S11-handleAccept, S9-handlePreAccept, S17-find-conflicts).

handlePrepareReply's sub-cases 3 and 4 carry textually identical guards, so sub-case 3 always wins and sub-case 4 never runs; bcastTryPreAccept is called only from sub-case 4, so handleTryPreAccept, findPreAcceptConflicts, handleTryPreAcceptReply and the possibleQuorum/deferMap machinery are unreachable dead code, and a recovery with weaker pre-accept support takes sub-case 5, which restarts phase 1 with the recovered value (a more conservative path) (S15-handlePrepareReply, S16-handleTryPreAccept, S17-find-conflicts, S18-handleTryPreAcceptReply).

handleTryPreAcceptReply's defer-cycle guard counts lb.possibleQuorum[tpar.AcceptorId] inside a loop over q, so the count can only be 0 or N and never equals N/2; the counting error has no reachable consequence because the handler is reachable only from the dead sub-case 4 (S18-handleTryPreAcceptReply, S15-handlePrepareReply).

recordInstanceMetadata writes bal at [0:4) and then vbal into the same bytes, with Status at byte [4] and Seq at [5:9); the direct check for claim C2-durable-record-preserves-written-fields confirmed in scope that the produced record carries vbal at offset 0 and no bal value, so the ballot context the function writes is not recoverable from the layout. No reader of the format exists in the snapshot and run.go passes durable = false, so the consequence is bounded to any future or external reader (S19-durable-record, S24-runReplica-epaxos).
the transconf branch inside Exec.strongconnect computes state.Conflict but performs no action, and run.go passes transconf = false (S20-exec, S24-runReplica-epaxos).

the N<=3 with Thrifty configuration skips the fast-path attribute-equality check while still committing at preAcceptOKs >= FastQuorumSize-1 = 1. The committed vector is the merge of the leader's own and the counted replies' (seq,deps) (mergeAttributes, installed into the bookkeeping before the branch choice), so the exemption does not publish the leader's own proposal vector; what it removes is the requirement that every counted reply already equal that merged vector, which is the step that otherwise either forces agreement or triggers the accept round that puts the merged vector on a majority. With exactly one counted peer the merged vector equals that peer's record in every compared component, and in an owner-led instance the peer skips precisely the leader's own row, so the fast quorum's two members both hold the committed vector at the same vbal. The residual exposure is therefore one component in a recovery-led phase 1 (leader != owner), where mergeAttributes ignores the leader's own row while the peer may hold a higher value for that row; that needs the peer to know more about the leader's own row than the leader does, which no read path establishes for a live leader (S7-attributes, S10-handlePreAcceptReply, S15-handlePrepareReply, S21-quorum-sizes).

handleCommit's NOOP re-proposal branch dereferences leader bookkeeping that message-created records do not have, so a legal NOOP commit for an instance the replica owns terminates the handler; the direct check for claim C4-noop-commit-without-bookkeeping confirmed in scope that a record created by a recovery-led PreAccept plus the commit raises a nil pointer dereference and leaves the instance uncommitted. The run loop has no recover, so the panic is inferred to end the process; the history that leaves a restarted owner in that state and the client-side consequence of the same NOOP recovery remain unread (S13-handleCommit, S9-handlePreAccept, S3-run-dispatch).

handleAcceptReply returns whenever a reply's ballot differs from the round's, so the nack branch behind that gate never runs and a peer that answers with a higher ballot is ignored rather than counted as a rejection; the direct check for claim C7 confirmed nacks 0 and no reaction, and the pre-accept side has no rejection signal either (PreAcceptReply copies the request's ballot and handlePreAccept returns silently for a smaller ballot), so progress after a rejection depends on the 10s execution timeout rather than on the handlers (S12-handleAcceptReply, S11-handleAccept, S4-execute-loop).

with recording enabled, the phase-1 entry records metadata through the recovering replica's own row while installing the instance under the owner's row, so a recovery-led phase 1 either records a different instance's ballot context or terminates on an absent record; the direct check for claim C9-durable-recorder-uses-the-instance-row confirmed the nil dereference with Durable true and an empty own row, and the case where that slot exists is still unread (S8-handlePropose-startPhase1, S19-durable-record).

the command value codec frames a value's length in a two-byte field on both sides, while the client's command size is configuration-driven; the three direct checks for claim C10-command-value-length-survives-the-wire confirmed in scope that a 70000-byte value is written as 70013 bytes but decoded as 4464 bytes with 4477 consumed, that the command following such a value in the same buffer decodes to garbage (op 197, an arbitrary key and a 53198-byte value), and that decoding a real PreAccept carrying such a value panics with makeslice: len out of range, which the receiver's reader has no recover for. The default configuration's 1000-byte commands never reach the boundary, and what a participant does after a displaced stream is unread (S37-state-value-codec, S38-client-command-size, S22-replica-listener).
core_overview.rationale: Both core relationships are traced through real entry points (client propose to phase 1 to pre-accept replies to fast or slow decision to commit install, and ballot promise to nack-driven prepare to recovery sub-cases) and their connection is stated in terms of the per-instance record, the highest-vbal reply rule, the committed short-circuit and the ballot comparison that rejects old replies. The remaining questions are local anomalies inside handlers rather than missing formation, authority-transition or old-work handling, so the overview is recorded as usable with those anomalies kept as open_details and as the first Candidate's discriminator.
